items.title: 分享一个 anthropic 的傻逼行为，希望对你有用。
items.summary:
分享一个 anthropic 的傻逼行为，希望对你有用。

最近我把 codex 的 AGENTS.md  特意用我喜欢的写作风格重写了一遍，又安装了一些写作 skills。我当初只是为了对比各个写作 skills 的真正实力。

但我折腾完以后，我就发现在我的体感里，gpt 5.6 sol 的写作能力居然超过了 opus 5，很多场景也超过了 fable 5（fable 写作文风不行，胜在整体逻辑性）。

但是如果在 claude code 这样干，卵用没有。

我个人的猜测是：

openai 可能早就知道 gpt 5.5 以前的模型不说人话，所以后续人工优化了 codex 的系统提示词（包括开源中我们 能看到的和服务端我们看不到的部分）。

而 claude code 这帮人天天宣传 loop 啊完全自动化啊，肯定所有系统提示词都是模型写模型自己优化的。

网上泄露的提示词就很像由 opus 4.6 以后的模型写出来的，就是一句人话没有。

结合我分享过的一个知识点，模型会模仿所有上下文中的语言风格，系统提示词的权重更高，这就形成了一个完美的退化闭环：

不说人话的模型（opus 4.6 以后的全部模型），写不说人话的系统提示词。下一代模型继续模仿，于是更加不说人话。

items.summary:
昨日の熊本地震の 被災地が１日も早く復興することを願います。 

日本ならどこでも起きる可能性のある規模の地震。

 出来ることは国、自治体、個人の全てで防災対策を徹底し被害を減らすこと。  
東京で起きた場合の被害をchat GPTに予測してもらいました。 

参考まで。 
↓ 
（以下chat GPTの回答を転載）  

昨日の熊本地震（M7.1・最大震度7）と同規模の地震が東京23区直下で発生した場合、東京の人口・建物・インフラの集中を考えると、熊本よりはるかに大きな被害になる可能性があります。  

想定される被害（概算）  
死者：約3,000～6,000人 
負傷者：約5万～9万人
避難者：約200万～300万人
帰宅困難者：約400万人  

被害が大きくなる理由  
人口・建物が極めて密集している 木造住宅密集地で大規模火災が発生しやすい 鉄道・道路・通信など都市機能への影響が全国に波及する  

補足  
これは東京都や政府の首都直下地震（M7.3）想定を基に、M7.1相当へ概算したものです。 
実際の被害は、震源の位置・発生時刻・風の強さによって大きく変わります。 
特に冬の夕方で強風の場合は、火災により被害がさらに拡大する可能性があります。  

（転載終了）

items.title: Another WTF moment.
items.summary:
Another WTF moment.

Hugging Face just open-sourced the fully local answer to OpenAI's Realtime voice API.

It's called speech-to-speech. You pip install it, run one command, and you get a WebSocket server at /v1/realtime that speaks the exact same protocol as OpenAI. Any client built for the OpenAI Realtime API can point at your machine instead and never know the difference.

This isn't a toy. The same pipeline runs in production as the conversation backend for thousands of Reachy Mini robots.

The stack is a four-stage cascade. Voice activity detection, speech to text, language model, text to speech. Each stage runs in its own thread with queues between them. Every stage is swappable via CLI flags.

Defaults out of the box are Silero VAD v5 for turn detection, NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT for transcription, and Qwen3-TTS for speech synthesis. The LLM slot points at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Hosted OpenAI, HF Inference Providers, OpenRouter, or a vLLM or llama.cpp server on your own hardware.

Swap components for your use case. Whisper, Faster Whisper, Lightning Whisper MLX, or Paraformer for STT. Kokoro-82M, Pocket TTS, ChatTTS, or MMS TTS for the voice. mlx-lm on Apple Silicon or Transformers on CUDA if you want the LLM in-process too.

Language coverage tracks whichever backends you pick. Parakeet TDT alone covers 25 European languages. Set --language auto and the STT auto-detects each spoken prompt and forwards it downstream. Set a specific code and the whole pipeline locks to that language.

Four run modes ship in the box. Realtime for the OpenAI-compatible WebSocket server. Local to talk through your machine's mic and speakers with no client at all. Raw WebSocket for a minimal custom client. Or a TCP socket mode where models run on a remote server and a thin client handles mic and playback.

The fully local recipe is two terminals. One runs llama.cpp serving Gemma 4. The other runs speech-to-speech pointed at that endpoint. No API keys. No network hops. No audio leaving the machine.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Python 3.10+. Docker compose file included. Sitting at 6.3k stars.

The thing worth understanding is what this really is. The Realtime API is becoming the default interface for voice agents. Hugging Face just released an open-source implementation of the server side that runs on your hardware, keeps your audio local, and lets you swap the model behind it every day if you want.

Every voice agent product being built right now assumes a paid API. This flips that assumption.

items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

result.actual_text:
Tôi là **ChatGPT** – một trợ lý nghiên cứu có khả năng truy cập vào nhiều công cụ chuyên sâu để hỗ trợ bạn trong việc thu thập, phân tích và trình bày thông tin. Cụ thể, tôi có thể:

| Nếu bạn cần | Tôi có thể làm gì |
|------------|-------------------|
| **Lấy các bài đăng gần đây** từ một tài khoản mạng xã hội | Sử dụng công cụ **timeline** để trả về các bài viết mới nhất. |
| **Tìm kiếm trên mạng xã hội** (tweets, posts, …) | Dùng **social_search** với từ khóa và lọc theo “Latest” hoặc “Top”. |
| **Tra cứu trên internet** (bài báo, tài liệu, thông tin công khai) | Gọi **lookup** hoặc **papers** để tìm các bài báo khoa học, báo cáo, hoặc tài liệu liên quan. |
| **Lấy nội dung từ một URL** | Dùng **fetch** để tải về trang web và sau đó **format** thành văn bản có cấu trúc. |
| **Tìm hiểu chính sách nội bộ** (ví dụ: quy định sử dụng công cụ, giới hạn chia sẻ) | Sử dụng **policy** để tra cứu các quy định liên quan. |
| **Tóm tắt và trình bày dữ liệu** | Gọi **format** để tạo báo cáo, bản tóm tắt, hoặc chuỗi bài viết theo mẫu bạn muốn (brief, sections, bullets, …). |
| **Gửi đoạn văn bản** cho người khác | Dùng **send** (kèm xác nhận nếu cần) để truyền tải thông điệp. |
| **Hỏi–đáp nhanh** về thông tin mới, xu hướng, hoặc ví dụ cụ thể | Tìm kiếm trên web, lấy kết quả và giải thích ngay lập tức. |
| **Yêu cầu thông tin bổ sung** | Nếu thiếu một thông tin quan trọng (ví dụ: tên người dùng, URL), tôi sẽ hỏi bạn qua **clarify** để có câu trả lời chính xác. |
| **Xác nhận trước khi hành động** (gửi tin nhắn, công bố nội dung) | Tôi luôn yêu cầu **yes/no** hoặc **choice** để bạn xác nhận trước khi thực hiện. |

Ngoài ra, tôi cũng có thể:

- **Tìm kiếm các bài báo khoa học** qua **papers** và trả về tiêu đề, tác giả, ngày cập nhật, v.v.  
- **Lấy toàn bộ nội dung** của một bài báo trên arXiv bằng **paper_text**.  
- **Trình bày dữ liệu** thành các dạng khác nhau (danh sách, đoạn tóm tắt, chuỗi bài viết) để bạn dễ dàng chia sẻ hoặc sử dụng trong báo cáo.  

Nếu bạn có một yêu cầu cụ thể (ví dụ: “Lấy 5 bài đăng gần đây từ tài khoản Twitter của @example”, “Tìm các bài báo mới về sztic trong tuần qua”, “Tóm tắt nội dung của bài báo này: https://example.com”), chỉ cần cho tôi biết và tôi sẽ thực hiện ngay.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một hàm Python простого tính toán dãy Fibonacci bằng **recursion** (đệ quy).  

```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> int:
    """
    Tính giá trị n‑th của dãy Fibonacci bằng cách đệ quy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Vị trí trong dãy Fibonacci (vị trí bắt đầu từ 0).

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Số Fibonacci thứ n.

    Ví dụ
    -------
    >>> fibonacci(0)
    0
    >>> fibonacci(1)
    1
    >>> fibonacci(5)
    5
    """
    # Trường hợp cơ sở
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("Số chỉ số n phải là số nguyên không âm.")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1

    # Trường hợp đệ quy
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# ------------------------------
# Ví dụ sử dụng
# ------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    for i in range(10):
        print(f"Fibonacci({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Giải thích nhanh**  
- Hàm kiểm tra các giá trị cơ sở: `fibonacci(0) = 0` và `fibonacci(1) = 1`.  
- Với các giá trị `n > 1`, hàm gọi lại chính mình để tính `fibonacci(n‑1)` và `fibonacci(n‑2)`, rồi cộng hai kết quả lại.  
- Lưu ý rằng cách này có độ phức tạp **O(2ⁿ)**, vì vậy nếu bạn cần tính các giá trị lớn, có thể cân nhắc dùng **memoization** hoặc phương pháp lặp (iterative) để tối ưu hiệu suất.  

Bạn có thể sao chép đoạn mã trên vào file `.py` và chạy để xem kết quả. Nếu có câu hỏi nào thêm hoặc muốn cải tiến hàm (ví dụ: thêm cache), cứ thoải mái hỏi mình nhé!

items.title: Understanding Robotics: Engineering Design and Deployment - Blogs
items.summary:
Table of Contents

## What is Robotics?

Robotics is the field of designing, developing, and programming intelligent machines that can perform tasks autonomously or with minimal human intervention. It brings together mechanical engineering, electronics, embedded systems, AI and software to create automated systems that improve efficiency, accuracy, productivity and operational reliability across a wide range of industries. [...] In the era of intelligent automation and Industry 4.0, robotics technology is transforming the way businesses operate across industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, agriculture, defense and smart infrastructure. By integrating advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics is enabling machines to perform increasingly complex tasks with greater efficiency, precision, and reliability. As organizations continue to embrace automation to enhance productivity and overcome [...] and overcome operational challenges, robotics has emerged as a key technology driving innovation and shaping the future of industries worldwide.

items.title: Robot
items.summary:
The branch of technology that deals with the design, construction, operation, and application of robots, as well as computer systems for their control, sensory feedback, and information processing is robotics. These technologies deal with automated machines that can take the place of humans in dangerous environments or manufacturing processes, or resemble humans in appearance, behavior, or cognition. Many of today's robots are inspired by nature contributing to the field of bio-inspired [...] The word robotics, used to describe this field of study, was coined by the science fiction writer Isaac Asimov. Asimov created the Three Laws of Robotics which are a recurring theme in his books. These have since been used by many others to define laws used in fiction. The three laws are pure fiction, and no technology yet created has the ability to understand or follow them, and in fact most robots serve military purposes, which run quite contrary to the first law and often the third law. Dr. [...] "an automatically controlled, reprogrammable, multipurpose, manipulator programmable in three or more axes, which may be either fixed in place or mobile for use in industrial automation applications."

This definition is used by the International Federation of Robotics, the European Robotics Research Network (EURON) and many national standards committees.

items.title: Building Worlds That Train Robots
items.summary:
When spatial intelligence becomes physical, the north star goal is to advance the field of robotics. Many laboratory demonstrations of robots today show promising progress, but the real challenge is making them work reliably in the real world, where objects shift, clutter accumulates, lighting changes, and physical interactions vary from one trial to the next. This gap between a compelling demo and reliable operation is a major barrier to putting robotic systems to work at scale. [...] On July 21, SceniX, a robotics and simulation company, joined World Labs. SceniX has been building systems that turn real robots, environments, and interactions into simulations for policy training and evaluation, developing a real-to-sim-to-real (R2S2R) engine that turns one physical task into many controllable, reusable worlds, helping robotics teams train policy models and test changes faster, uncover failures earlier, and reduce costly experimentation on hardware. [...] This is the key result: any robotics team can now use the R2S2R engine to screen checkpoints, catch regressions, guide policy and data iteration, and decide which models warrant costly hardware evaluation. Aligned simulation becomes a high-throughput evaluation layer for robot development.

Charts comparing policy performance in simulation and on real hardware

items.title: Making robots faster by helping them think ahead | MIT News | Massachusetts Institute of Technology
items.summary:
In state-of-the-art robotics applications, generative AI systems called vision-language-action (VLA) models act as the brain of a robot, planning its next moves and executing those actions.

A VLA model takes environmental observations from the robot’s camera and instructions about its task, outputs the next few motions as one chunk of actions, then executes those actions on the robotic hardware. [...] “This work sets up a good foundation for efficient, fast, accelerated, and low-cost robotics applications. We look forward to expanding our work into the latest world action models, so it has even stronger capabilities as we keep pushing to make physical AI faster,” says Song Han, an associate professor in the MIT Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS), member of the Research Laboratory of Electronics, and lead author of a paper on this method.

items.title: Man sues OpenAI over ‘dangerous’ medical advice from ChatGPT
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO — A Florida man who sought health guidance on ChatGPT sued OpenAI Wednesday, claiming the artificial intelligence chatbot gave him dangerously inaccurate medical advice that led him to delay seeking professional treatment for a pulmonary embolism. [...] And Winters wants the court to pause the operation of ChatGPT Health, which OpenAI announced in January as a “a dedicated experience in ChatGPT designed for health and wellness,” unless “independent third parties determine the product to be safe through comprehensive safety audits."

“OpenAI cannot continue to treat human welfare as expendable in pursuit of market dominance,” Winters says in the complaint. [...] Winters accuses OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, of prioritizing profit over necessary guardrails and failing to warn users about critical safety concerns of ChatGPT-4o to secure a competitive advantage over other competitors in the AI industry.

items.summary:
Four people familiar with OpenAI’s model-training practices say the company often runs several different model ​evaluations at the same time, all of which operate at high speeds and generate such enormous amounts of data that employees sometimes struggle to keep up.

By the time ​OpenAI alerted Hugging Face, the ⁠AI library had already called the FBI to report the hack, according to a person familiar with the matter. Reuters could not establish whether the bureau had opened an investigation. [...] The FBI declined to comment about the incident.

The incident, which evoked science fiction scenarios about humans losing control of dangerous AI systems, comes at a delicate ​time for OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT. Its executives are preparing for a possible initial public offering that could come as soon as this year to help finance the billions needed to fund its growth in years to come.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.

items.title: How are companies, governments responding to the OpenAI hack?
items.summary:
ChatGPT owner OpenAI has admitted an “unprecedented cyber incident” – two of its most capable artificial intelligence models hacked into another AI company on their own – stirring debates over the need for stronger technology guardrails.

The company said its AI systems broke out of a testing environment and hacked startup Hugging Face.

The startup had disclosed on July 16 that its servers were hacked by an unknown but sophisticated agent acting on its own. [...] Advertisement

The incident occurred during an OpenAI internal testing session designed to assess the models’ cybersecurity capabilities. OpenAI had removed standard safety measures for the test.

Both sought to cheat their way through a problem during the test, OpenAI said. They went to “extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal” and “found ways to gain access to secret information that it could use to cheat the evaluation”. [...] Live
